collapse, while the cost in science is theoretical stagnation or error retention."],"overturn_conditions":["If it can be shown that choosing the 'tested' bridge logically entails an expectation of its without knowledge of the final outcome."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_003","SRC_007"],"transfer_claims":["Just as an engineer chooses the bridge that passed the hardest load tests without knowing the expectation of repetition."]},"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on Popper's terms not as an inductive inference that the future will resemble the past, but as a induction is rejected) and the pragmatic context of action. By treating the choice of theory as a methodological rule rather than a probabilistic calculation, scientists can prefer Theory A over Theory B because A has higher content and has survived tests that would have falsified it, whereas B has not. This preference does not assert A is 'true' or 'probably true,' but that A is the best available target for further critical testing, aligning with the goal of increasing verisimilitude.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
